content:
alex: Hey team — getting a customer escalation: after we onboarded the new model variant redwood-alpha-onnx-q4_0 (rolled out to hosted last night) they're seeing p99 jump from ~320ms to ~1.6s for 6-8k token requests. Root request ts 1765154321. cc @raj @mia

mia: Ack. Got the ticket link?

alex: https://support.redwood.ai/t/CR-8821 (private) — customer provided traces and sample repro. They say short contexts (<=512) are fine, long contexts hit the spike.

raj: Noted. Any changes other than ONNX quantization + new tokenizer?

alex: Two changes: 1) model converted to ONNX with Q4_0 kernels, 2) tokenizer moved from hf/tokenizers -> tok-fast-fork (slightly different BOS/EOS handling). Onboarding script: `rctl deploy-model --name redwood-alpha-onnx-q4_0 --variant canary --enable-quant`

support-bot: [automated] Alert created: support/CR-8821 escalated to SRE. Incident ID: INC-2026-034.

mia: I'll pull p95/p99 graphs (console).

mia: p50 stable, p95 up ~1.2x for long ctx, p99 for long ctx ~5x. Host metrics show CPU spike on host runtime, GPU utilization normal.

raj: Interesting — CPU spike suggests tokenizer or pre/post processing. Can we capture an end-to-end trace? request-id from customer: req_0a9f3c

alex: Customer included a flamegraph (attached). The time is spent in tokenization and prefix/kv-cache serialization.

eva: I see two suspects: 1) tokenizer change adds regex passes per chunk, 2) ONNX path adds extra CPU-side rematerialization for attention KV handling for long contexts. Need repro.

alex: Repro steps from customer (they provided script):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-onnx-q4_0","input": "<8k tokens payload>", "max_tokens": 64, "stream": false}'
```
They say 1.6s p99, previous model redwood-alpha-1.3b returned ~340ms.

raj: Can we repro internally? I'll run the script in canary cluster.

sre-ops: Spawning canary job on cluster-canary-2 now, using customer's payload (sanitized).

sre-ops: Repro succeeded. Host CPU stays high during tokenization and prefill. I captured logs:
```
[2026-03-10T21:02:12Z] tokenization: chunk_count=40, time_ms=742
[2026-03-10T21:02:12Z] kv_prefill: pages=12, serialize_ms=510
[2026-03-10T21:02:12Z] total_server_ms=1618
```

mia: That's the same pattern as customer. Tokenization ~740ms, KV serialize ~510ms. Older model: tokenization ~120ms, serialize ~80ms.

eva: So both tokenizer and kv serialization are ~4-6x slower. Which change triggered KV serialization increase? ONNX runtime variant maybe changed how KV cache is stored (different dtype or layout) causing expensive conversions.

raj: Good angle. I'll diff the model build artifacts.

raj: Found it — ONNX export uses packed KV format with int8 indices for quant kernels, so we added an on-the-fly re-layout step to convert to runtime layout. That conversion is CPU-bound and scales with context length.

eva: And tokenizer: the tok-fast-fork added a normalization pass per 128-token chunk (regex NFKC) which wasn't present before. That explains chunk_count * regex cost.

alex: Customer impact: long-context generation p99 up, some timeouts on their side (they have 2s client timeout). They asked for mitigation or rollback.

mia: Mitigation options: 1) Rollback to previous model variant (redwood-alpha-1.3b) for affected customers 2) Patch ONNX export to emit runtime layout (cheap) instead of converting at runtime 3) Disable new tokenizer or fall back to compat tokenizer for canary.

sre-ops: We can hotpatch a route rule to map that customer to compat model variant within 10m. Would require config change: `route.override(customer_id=CR-8821, model=redwood-alpha-1.3b)`

raj: Quick fix: route override + mark redwood-alpha-onnx-q4_0 as paused for hosted canary. Longer fix: change export to store runtime KV layout; PR incoming.

mia: Customer wants immediate fix. I'll propose route override and re-run canary after patch.

alex: I've proposed the rollback to customer and they accepted. They asked for ETA on permanent fix.

raj: Workplan: (1) apply route override for CR-8821 now (2) pause canary rollout (3) PR to exporter to write runtime layout (should be <48h) (4) remove tok-fast-fork or add fast-path without NFKC for long contexts (investigating).

sre-ops: Route override applied at 1765157820 — routing logs show requests now hitting redwood-alpha-1.3b and p99 back to normal ~360ms.

support-bot: [automated] Action logged: route.override for CR-8821 applied by sre-ops.

mia: Confirming metrics: customer p99 back in range within one minute after override.

eva: Creating two follow-ups: ENG-ONNX-145 (exporter change) and ENG-TOKEN-67 (tokenizer fast-path for long contexts). Assigning to @raj and @eva respectively.

raj: I'll start exporter PR, including microbench for kv layout conversion. Putting a feature-flag to disable conversion at runtime.

alex: Customer updated: happy for now, asked for postmortem + timeline. They're ok with the route override if we deliver fix within 72 hours.

mia: I'll draft a short incident note for the customer and internal postmortem.

support-bot: [automated] Incident INC-2026-034 status: mitigated. Postmortem required.

alex: Thanks all. Next steps: raj/ev a to deliver PRs, mia to send PM note and customer update, sre-ops keep the route override until the exporter is deployed.

sre-ops: Will monitor for any other customers affected by canary. No other spikes so far.

alex: Assigning owners in ticket. Closing thread here — will re-open if regression recurs. :thumbsup:
